newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products broadly flat in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products broadly flat in slow trade.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were broadly steady with little trading seen.
Gas oil outright prices firmed 75 cents in line with August IPE, which closed at $167.75 a tonne.
Business was thin. As in northern Europe most attention was concentrated on efforts to widen a stubbornly narrow heating oil/diesel price quotation.
Refiners say they need at least another $5 on top of the $5 spread in the Mediterranean in order to make EN590 production profitable.
Italian heating oil was assessed steady at $2 to $2.50 over the high cif Med quotations basis Genoa, with Russian gas oil around $1 or $1.50 dearer.
High sulphur fuel was held up by bunker demand that could not be satisfied with the grades available.
Buyers were reported looking to the NWE market, where an imminent influx of Russian cracked fuel may serve to satisify their appetite.
They were heard bidding from $93-$96 for delivery into Italy, with some traders believing they will pay more.
Russian cracked and straight-run cargoes were coming over the Black Sea horizon at about their normal frequency.
Gasoline continues to be $3-4 a tonne stronger than NWE levels at $210-212 cif for eurograde material, but with little physical material available liquidity has been limited.
